text: getDefense() returns defense * 0.8 in HEAVY_STANCE and defense unmodified in every other stance — the source line behind the ledger's 'Heavy def x0.8'. Confirmed a second time by InventoryUI.as:1964 setting defModifier = 0.8 for heavy in the gear-comparison panel.

lane_impact: L2 skills-meters — completes the packet's focus-is-the-reload-meter claim, which only carried the flat slashusage. L5 combat-core — this is the actual crit economy: Light crits often for 1.5x, Heavy crits rarely for 1.2x, and that tension is the stance meta.
text: The Focus/reload drain is stance-scaled, and landing a crit costs the entire bar. deductReloadBar() first zeroes a full bar, then subtracts slashUsage/2 in Light, slashUsage in Balanced and Reversed, and slashUsage*1.5 in Heavy and Dual. So Light rebuilds Focus twice as fast per slash as Balanced and three times as fast as Heavy — and every crit resets the meter to zero.

lane_impact: L8 ui-hud and L6 art-anim-audio-feel — a rebuild that maps [0, maxreload] onto the bar will feel wrong even with every number right, because the OG hides the first 24 frames. This is exactly the 'dynamic HUD feel' the ledger's :235 blocker ② says is uncatalogued.
text: The Focus bar's displayed fill is not reload/maxreload. bonusReload() pushes the bar with updateReload((this.reload - 24) / (this.maxreload - 24)), so the bar maps [24, maxreload] onto [0,1] and the first 24 frames of charge are invisible. bonusReload also grants a flat +6 reload, clamped to maxreload.

cite: reference/decompiled/shs3_android_payload/scripts/StatsManager.as:4222 (rand), :4279-4295 (switch eq/gte/gt/lt/lte/not/default), :4173 (default gte); authored <comp> census over reference/extracted/android/*.bin
lane_impact: L4 enemies-ai, L1 world-exploration, L-quests-story, L-economy. The ledger treats conditions as flat 'has item X' gates; the shipped evaluator is a six-operator comparison plus a probability primitive, and 'lte' is declared but never authored.
quote: 4279:switch(comparison) 4281:case "eq": 4283:case "gte": 4285:case "gt": 4287:case "lt": 4289:case "lte": 4291:case "not": 4293:default: return false;
text: The <condition> evaluator's comparison enum is seven operators, not the two the packet names. StatsManager.checkCondition special-cases 'rand' first and then runs a full switch: eq, gte, gt, lt, lte, not, with default returning false. Authored usage across the whole Android corpus is 13 sites: nodedata rand x1; achievementdata not x1; questdata eq x5, gt x1, gte x2, not x1; uidata gte x1, lt x1, not x1. An absent <comp> defaults to 'gte'. Every <condition> in nodedata, questdata, uidata and achievementdata draws on the same evaluator, so any of them can be made probabilistic, negated or bounded.

cite: reference/decompiled/shs3_android_payload/scripts/XMLBG.as:10 (groundY=400), :12 (flatGround=true), :58-140 (override-if-present constructor) against the full tag histogram of reference/extracted/android/123_Mobile_BGData.bin (49 records, zero groundy / flatground / gwrap / fgwrap tags)
lane_impact: L6 art-anim + L5 combat-core. A single authored ground line at y=400 for every scene in the game is a hard layout constant a recreation can bake in, and it is stronger than the banked reading of groundY as a mere default.
quote: XMLBG.as:10 'internal var groundY:int = 400;' :12 'internal var flatGround:Boolean = true;' :66 'if(xml.groundy.toString() != "") { this.groundY = xml.groundy; }' - and <groundy> occurs 0 times across all 49 <bg> records.
text: groundY = 400 and flatGround = true are not per-background defaults that locations override - they are global constants for every location in the game. XMLBG's constructor overrides each field only when the matching tag is present (<groundy>, <flatground>), and across all 49 <bg> records in 123_Mobile_BGData neither tag occurs even once. The same is true of <gwrap> and <fgwrap>, so groundLayerWrap and foregroundLayerWrap are universally 1600.

lane_impact: L6 art-anim. STRENGTHENS android-blobs/parallax-and-dof-contract, which reads the declaration site only and therefore reports groundLayerBlur=4 as a uniform plane property. It is not: it is a per-layer rule with an index cutoff, and four of the 49 backgrounds have ground layers past the cutoff. Also note only those two layers get cacheAsBitmap, so the blur is baked once and the sharp ground layers stay live.
quote: 248 `if(i <= 2 && groundLayerBlur != 0)` 249 `{` 250 `ColorCode.blur(mc,groundLayerBlur);` 251 `mc.cacheAsBitmap = true;` 252 `}`  — every other plane guards only on `if(<plane>LayerBlur != 0)` with no index test. bgdata gcount reaches 4 (BG_ForestSpooky, BG_Graveyard, BG_TempleRuinsFog, BG_DungeonFog), so layers 3 and 4 there are authored to render SHARP.
text: The ground plane is the one exception to the blur ladder: groundLayerBlur is applied only to ground layers 1 and 2, while farthest, far, playerPlane and foreground blur every layer they own — so a recreation that blurs all ground layers at 4 is wrong.

lane_impact: L6 art-anim + method. This is the reason I refuted android-blobs/foreground-layer-occludes-the-fighters: no A1 frame can tell you whether an occluding band is ground_i or fg_i, because the code never decides — the FLA author did. Two ways to settle any such question, both cheap: measure the band's pixel displacement against the fighter's across a pan (gscroll=1 vs fgscroll=2), or decode the named children of the relevant BG_* symbol in the decrypted 120_Mobile_BGResource. It also tells a rebuilder that the 874 layer slots in bgdata are counts of pre-placed children, not a runtime spawn list.

lane_impact: L6 art-anim-audio-feel and L1 combat-core: this is the recovery-window table for every slash. Two counters exist — currentAnimationDuration (the @d + code tail, MCSCharacter.as:1316) and frameList.length (MCSCharacter.as:1334) — and the gap between them IS the pose latch. It is the correct replacement for the ledger's '15fps pose latch' shorthand and for the refuted claim art-anim-audio-feel/hold-frames-are-authored-in-data.
ledger_text: **Ready (strongest slice):** 15fps pose latch; walk + run gaits; per-stance slash frames; hit-stagger; death collapse; proportions; combat-crouch idle;
quote: AnimData.as:15 `this.duration = xml.@d;` · :25 `case "light_afterslashpose":` :26 `this.duration += 10;` · :28-40 the twelve `case MCSActor.*SLASH_POSE:` then :41 `this.duration += 10;` · :43-52 the ten `case MCSActor.*FALLSLASH_END/*JUMPSLASH_LAND:` then :53 `this.duration += 15;` · :55-56 `case "sheathesword": case "sheathesword3":` :57 `+= 24;` · :58-65 `case "deathenemy"/"deathnohand"/"deathnohead"/"defeatedanimationv2"/"death"/"gob_death"/KNEEGROIN_VICTIM:` :66 `+= 6;` · MCSCharacter.as:1316 `if(this.frameCounter < this.currentAnimationDuration)` · :1334 `if(this.frameCounter < this.currentAnimation.frameList.length)`
text: The real per-animation hold table is a hard-coded switch in AnimData's constructor, not the XML. AnimData.as:15 copies @d verbatim from the data (which always equals len(<f>)), then :25-141 ADDS the tail: +10 for 'light_afterslashpose' and for all twelve *SLASH_POSE variants, +15 for the five *FALLSLASH_END and five *JUMPSLASH_LAND, +24 for 'sheathesword'/'sheathesword3' and 'gotlauncheddownedend', +6 for the whole death set, and ~25 more single cases running up to +50. This is the table a motion rebuild actually needs, and no amount of data extraction will find it.

cite: reference/extracted/bindata/*.bin - all 19 animdata blobs, parsed with `<anim\b([^>]*)>(.*?)</anim>` and compared against the strict `<anim i="X" d="N">` form
lane_impact: art-anim-audio-feel: strengthens art-anim-audio-feel/24fps-keyframe-stream from a 2-blob sample to a proven universal across all 487 authored animations - the data genuinely holds no hold frames anywhere, and every latch is code-added by AnimData's duration tails. Also a standing measurement warning for any lane re-deriving animation counts or durations from the bindata XML: parse `<anim\b[^>]*>`, never `<anim i=".." d="..">`, or you lose the looping animations and invent hold frames that are not there.
quote: robust parse: total anims parsed 487, mismatches d != number-of-<f> : 0. Strict parse drops 38 of the 158 anims in 108_1t4635s0.bin (both `walk` d=20 and `light_run` d=9 are missed) and reports ~96 false mismatches such as ogre_swingdownhit d=5 vs 3 frames.
text: The d-equals-frame-count invariant holds across ALL 19 web animdata blobs (487/487 anims, zero mismatches), but only under a robust parse: ~100 <anim> tags carry an extra attribute after d, so a strict regex silently drops them and manufactures phantom hold frames.

cite: own DefineSound parse of the decoded reference/extracted/android/122_Mobile_SoundResource.bin (id 9 samples=3809, rate 11025) vs afinfo on the MP3 carved from that same tag
lane_impact: L-art-anim-audio-feel: every ported SFX/music duration in this survey must be re-derived as samples/11025 from the SWF tag, not from afinfo. The stems are 80.013 s and 45.741 s, not 79.872 and 45.760; slash1 is 0.345 s, not 0.572 s. Timing a WebAudio recreation to the afinfo numbers would run the whole SFX bed 66% long.
quote: DefineSound id=9 fmt=MP3 rate=11025 16bit mono samples=3809 bytes=1153  ·  afinfo: 'estimated duration: 0.572000 sec', 'audio packets: 11' (11 x 576 = 6,336 decoded samples)
text: Flash plays the DefineSound sampleCount, not the raw MP3 stream length, so afinfo durations overstate the in-game length: slash1 is 3,809 samples at 11025 Hz = 0.345 s, while afinfo estimates 0.572 s from the same bytes.
